_meta.role: Bridge File - connects the ML taxonomy (Domain -> Issue) to legal truth (Act -> Section). Holds issue prototype texts (Module 2) and issue-to-provision references (Module 3).
_meta.population_status: SKELETON - no issues populated. The 22-issue taxonomy remains WORKING pending user sign-off (docs/issue_support_review.md); issues enter this file only after sign-off, and issues at provision_research_required only after their research completes.
governance: CLAUDE.md Section 6.3-6.4 (prototypes are Module 2's similarity corpus), 6.7 Layer B (provision_relevance_rationale is human-curated), 6.9 (this file is NOT training data - Module 2 is not a trained classifier), 7.3 (reference integrity).
Reference integrity: every (act_id, section_id) pair in provision_references must resolve to a real entry in acts_and_sections.json. Legal text is never duplicated here.

provision_relevance_rationale explains why a provision is mapped to an issue TYPE (curated, written by a human). It is not generated at request time and must never be merged with the request-time issue_match_reason (Layer A).
consumed_by: Module 2 (Issue Detector): at service startup, fits its own in-memory TF-IDF vectorizer over ALL prototype_texts across all issues (no .pkl saved); per request, compares the scenario only against prototypes of issues whose domain_id matches Module 1's predicted domain.
Module 3 (Legal Intelligence Engine): given the detected issue_id, reads provision_references and resolves them against acts_and_sections.json.
knowledge_base_loader: loads and reference-validates this file at startup (read-only at runtime).

<issue_id>._id_rule: issue_id is a stable snake_case string from the signed-off taxonomy, e.g. 'otp_fraud'. Must belong to exactly one domain.
<issue_id>.issue_id: string - MUST equal the object key. Explicit self-identifier so records are safe to validate, iterate, and pass around detached from their key.
<issue_id>.taxonomy_status: enum: 'working' | 'provision_research_required' | 'taxonomy_supported' | 'rejected' | 'merged' - governance state carried from docs/issue_support_review.md. Population rule: an issue enters this file only after user taxonomy sign-off, and issues at 'provision_research_required' only after their research completes.
<issue_id>.domain_id: string - one of the 5 approved domain IDs: 'cyber_fraud' | 'consumer_issues' | 'traffic_enforcement' | 'workplace_wage' | 'contractual_disputes'
<issue_id>.display_name: string - citizen-facing issue name, e.g. 'OTP / Financial Impersonation Fraud'
<issue_id>.issue_definition: string - the what-happened scenario definition (mirrors the signed-off taxonomy definition; issues represent what happened, never a desired remedy/procedure/portal)
prototype_texts: array of 3-5 strings - curated, well-differentiated citizen-voice descriptions of how this issue typically sounds. Module 2's similarity corpus. NOT training data; NOT drawn from training_data_v1.csv. Must be written to keep sibling issues separable (see flagged weak boundaries in docs/issue_support_review.md Section 6).

provision_references.section_id: string - must resolve under that act's sections
provision_references.provision_relevance_rationale: string - Layer B (CLAUDE.md Section 6.7): human-curated reason this provision is associated with this issue type. Not request-time generated; not legal certainty.

_schema._runtime_note: Module 3 must apply the citizen-facing eligibility check (manually_verified AND in_force) AFTER resolving each reference - a reference existing here never implies the provision is verified or returnable. If no referenced provision is eligible, Module 3 reports the explicit safe state (legal_information_status = 'no_verified_provision_available').

otp_fraud.issue_definition: The citizen was manipulated - typically by a caller or message impersonating a bank, wallet, or official - into revealing an OTP, PIN, or banking credential, followed by (or aimed at) an unauthorized financial transaction.
prototype_texts: Someone called me pretending to be from my bank and asked for the OTP that came on my phone, and after I told them money was taken from my account.
A caller claiming to be from bank or wallet customer support tricked me into sharing an OTP or PIN and an unauthorized transaction happened right after that.
I received a phone call about KYC verification or card blocking, the person asked me to read out the code sent by SMS, and then money got debited from my account without my permission.
A fraudster acting like customer care of a payment app made me share a verification code on call and immediately transferred money out of my wallet or account.

provision_references.provision_relevance_rationale: This provision is mapped to this issue type because the curated issue definition involves another person fraudulently using the citizen's electronic authentication details, such as an OTP or password, to carry out a transaction.

This provision is mapped to this issue type because the curated issue definition involves alleged impersonation of a bank, company, or official through a communication device in order to deceive the citizen.

online_impersonation.issue_definition: Someone poses online or via a phone/digital channel as a real person, official, or organization - a fake profile, a fake officer call, a spoofed business identity - to deceive, intimidate, or defraud, where the scenario does not center on OTP extraction or a fake login page.
prototype_texts: Someone has created a fake social media profile using my name and photos and is contacting people I know to ask them for money.
A person called claiming to be a police officer or government official and threatened action against my family member unless money was paid to settle a case.
Somebody is pretending to be my employer or a senior person on a messaging app and instructing colleagues to make urgent purchases or money transfers.
A fake profile pretending to be a real company or a known person deceived me during online conversations and took money from me under false pretences.

provision_references.provision_relevance_rationale: This provision is mapped to this issue type because the curated issue definition concerns alleged cheating by pretending to be another person, official, or organization through a communication device or computer resource.

This provision is mapped to this issue type because impersonation scenarios can involve the fraudulent use of another person's identity features, such as their name, photographs, or credentials, to pose as them online.

phishing.issue_definition: The citizen received fake links, websites, login pages, emails, or SMS engineered to harvest credentials or payments - for example a fake bank page, a fake KYC-update link, or a fake bill-payment or delivery-fee page.
prototype_texts: I got an SMS or email with a link that opened a page looking exactly like my bank or a government website and it asked me to enter my card details or login password.
A message warned that my electricity or KYC or SIM will be blocked today and asked me to click a link and update my details, and the link led to a fake page.
I clicked a link offering a gift, refund, or prize, and it asked me to fill in my phone number, bank details, or card information on a form.
A fake payment request or fake refund link was sent to me on a UPI or messaging app, designed so that accepting it would take money from my account.

provision_references.provision_relevance_rationale: This provision is mapped to this issue type because phishing pages and links are typically designed to capture and fraudulently use the citizen's passwords, card details, or other unique identification features.

This provision is mapped to this issue type because a fake website, page, or message that pretends to be a real bank, company, or government service in order to deceive the citizen involves alleged cheating by personation through a computer resource.

identity_theft.display_name: Identity Theft / Misuse of Personal Identifiers
identity_theft.issue_definition: The citizen's identity documents or identifiers (Aadhaar, PAN, photographs, credentials) have been misused by another person - for example loans, SIM cards, wallet accounts, or other services obtained in the citizen's name without their knowledge.
prototype_texts: A SIM card or mobile connection was issued in my name in another place which I never applied for, probably using a copy of my Aadhaar.
My credit report shows a loan or credit card that I never took, and someone appears to have used my PAN details to get it.
A wallet or bank account was opened using my identity documents and it is being used for transactions, and recovery agents are now calling me.
Photocopies of my identity documents given somewhere were misused to obtain a connection, account, or loan in my name without my knowledge.

provision_references.provision_relevance_rationale: This provision is mapped to this issue type because the curated issue definition concerns the fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's unique identification features - such as identity documents, numbers, or credentials - by someone else.
